Or maybe the arrow keys control a cursor on the grid of gray squares, and the cursor is invisible? Or maybe the arrow keys do nothing, and the actual interaction is MOUSE (clicking on a green blob to pick it up / click to move it) and ACTION7 (some kind of special action).

Bounding box rows 18-20 (3 rows), columns 18-20 (3 columns) = 9 cells, but 12 pixels... hmm, the boundary corners are [18,18],[18,19],[19,20],[20,20] — this is a clockwise outer perimeter, and for a staircase shape: row 18: columns 18-19? Let me try reading the ascii locally to check the shape.
Actually, the green shape might be a small "creature" (like a 3x3 with a notch). There are 5 of them.

So each green blob has 4 gray corner pixels around it (part of a "socket"?). Interesting: these w pixels are single light-gray cells at the corners of the 4x4 cell where the green blob sits.
So the grid: each "cell" is a 4x4 region. The gray squares are 4x4 blocks. The green blobs sit in 4x4 cells (rows 18-21, columns 17-20, etc.), with single gray pixels at the corners.
Hmm, wait, actually the green blob at rows 18-20, columns 18-20 plus the corner pixels at (18,17),(18,20)... let me try to map it: the cell region is rows 17-20, columns 17-20 (4x4). The gray square occupies all 16 cells. The green blob occupies 12 of the 16 cells? No wait — the green blob is 12 pixels, and the 4 corner pixels are w (light gray). And the boundary [[18,18],[18,19],[19,20],[20,20]] is consistent with a 4x4 square with corners cut: the top edge spans columns 18-19 (row 17? no...). Hmm, the top-left corner of the boundary is [18,18]... but the w pixel is at (18,17). Let me read the ascii of the region rows 17-22, columns 16-22 to check.
In any case, the green object is a 4x4 "corner-cut square" — probably a collectible or the player.
Now, what's the goal? Probably: collect all the green blobs (e.g., click them, or move the player onto them). The arrow keys didn't move anything visible. Maybe the player is the white room itself? No, that's not it.
